report.summary: Reviewed graph_brief.py chunk 2 (lines 281+) — rendered layer logic and render_brief. Claims checked: budget enforcement, priority order, artifact filtering, public API only, document layer, header reserve, truncation notice, render_brief never raises.
risks: line 286 | medium | _HEADER_RESERVE is used but not defined in this chunk; if it is not defined in the earlier part of the file, the function will NameError at runtime. | Check the definition of _HEADER_RESERVE in the first chunk or the module globals.

line 383 | medium | The budget check `spent + len(head) + len(line) + 1 > budget_chars` uses `budget_chars` but it is not defined in this chunk; it must be a parameter or closure variable. If not, it raises NameError. | Verify that `budget_chars` is a parameter of graph_brief.

line 448 | low | The docstring for render_brief says it returns "" if there is nothing to say, but the function returns graph_brief(...).text, which may be a non-empty string even if there are no structural facts (the header still says 'No structural facts available'). | The claim is about failure degradation, not about empty content; the code degrades to "" on exception, which matches.

This could cause a slight overshoot if headers are large, but the reserve is meant to cover that. | Verify the size of _HEADER_RESERVE; the logic is consistent with the comment.

line 358 | low | The `_emit` function adds `spent += len(head)` only after successfully keeping at least one line, but if the first line does not fit, the head is not counted; the header space is reserved up front, so this is consistent. | The logic is correct.

line 340 | low | The comment says 'Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood' but the neighbourhood filtering is not visible in this chunk; the claim is uncheckable. | The comment is about a prior bug; the current code does filter reverse edges.

handoff.purpose: Renders the three layers (imports, symbols, documents) under a character budget, assembles the final brief, and provides a never-raising render_brief wrapper.

symbols.name: _emit
symbols.note: Closure inside graph_brief; renders a layer if it fits under the budget, tracks counts and dropped lines, and stores rendered text in the `rendered` dict.

symbols.name: graph_brief
symbols.note: Builds the structural brief: iterates over rels and neighbours, emits IMPORTS, SYMBOLS, DOCUMENTS layers, composes the header, and returns a GraphBrief dataclass instance.

symbols.name: render_brief
symbols.note: Convenience wrapper that calls graph_brief and returns its text, or empty string on any exception.

claims.text: Render a layer if it fits.
claims.why: The function checks `if spent + len(head) + len(line) + 1 > budget_chars: break` and only adds lines that fit.

claims.text: Called in PRIORITY order, not display order.
claims.why: The calls are imports, symbols, documents, and the display order is symbols, imports, documents (line 419).

claims.text: Priority matters because the layers are wildly different sizes: the 1-hop symbol layer around offload.py alone is 495 lines, and emitting it first consumed the entire budget and dropped the import layer -- the smallest and most valuable of the three, and the only one that answers 'what will I break'.
claims.why: The claim refers to a specific measurement (495 lines) and a prior incident, not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Small high-value layers are rendered first and DISPLAYED in reading order.
claims.why: The render order is imports, symbols, documents; the display order is symbols, imports, documents (line 419).

claims.text: The header is written last but must not escape the budget, so its space is reserved up front.
claims.why: `spent = _HEADER_RESERVE` is set before any rendering, and the header is composed after the layers.

claims.text: A brief that overshoots by exactly the size of its own preamble is the kind of off-by-a-section that only shows up as a truncated prompt at the far end.
claims.why: The claim is about a possible failure mode; the code reserves header space, but the exact size of _HEADER_RESERVE is not visible here.

claims.text: Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood.
claims.why: The code filters `reverse.get(rel)` with `_is_artefact`, and the comment explains why.

claims.text: Measured: the first brief for shift.py had no artefact neighbour left and still printed '<- imported by runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py', because a reverse edge is read straight off the index and never passed through the walk.
claims.why: The claim is about a past measurement and a specific file; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: '->' imports, '<-' is imported by.
claims.why: The code builds lines like `f"{rel} -> {', '.join(marked)}"` and `f"{rel} <- imported by {', '.join(inc)}"`.

claims.text: '{DEEP_EDGE_MARK}' marks an edge that exists only inside a function body -- a change there still breaks the importer.
claims.why: The meaning of DEEP_EDGE_MARK and the deep module analysis are defined elsewhere; this chunk only applies the mark.

claims.text: PUBLIC API ONLY for a neighbour. What a caller may use from another module is its public surface; its private helpers are not callable and listing them cost 495 lines around offload.py -- enough to consume the whole budget on names nobody is allowed to reference.
claims.why: The code calls `file_symbols(path, include_private=False)` for neighbours, and the comment explains the rationale.

claims.text: If a name is not listed under its file, it does not exist in that file. Do not import it.
claims.why: The claim depends on the correctness of file_symbols, which is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: ``document_links_reverse`` is keyed BY THE CODE FILE, which is the lookup wanted here -- a scan of the forward map would be O(all pages) per lane.
claims.why: The code uses `rev.get(rel)` which is a reverse lookup by code file.

claims.text: Both keys are absent unless the document layer is enabled, so this section vanishes rather than lying when it is off.
claims.why: The document layer is only emitted if `include_docs` is true, and the index keys are only present then.

claims.text: Wikilinks from a page INTO code are a separate relation with its own layer, and are only forward-keyed.
claims.why: The code uses `wiki.items()` and filters by `set(described) & set(rels)`, which is a forward lookup.

claims.text: A page that describes one of these files. Its claims are a PROMISE, not evidence -- where the code disagrees, the document is the bug.
claims.why: The claim is a policy statement; the code only lists pages, it does not compare code and documentation.

claims.text: DISPLAY order, independent of the priority order the layers were rendered in: symbols first because 'what exists' is what a writer needs before anything else, then who reaches whom, then what has been promised.
claims.why: The sections list is `["symbols", "imports", "documents"]`.

claims.text: BUDGET: truncated -- ... Absence below is NOT evidence of absence in the repo.
claims.why: The header appends this message when `dropped` is non-empty, and the message includes the caveat.

claims.text: :func:`graph_brief` as text, or "" if there is nothing to say.
claims.why: The function returns graph_brief(...).text, which may be non-empty even when there are no structural facts (the header says 'No structural facts available'). The claim 'nothing to say' is ambiguous; the code only returns "" on exception.

claims.text: The convenience a provider calls: it must never raise into a lane, so a failure to describe the graph degrades to no description.
claims.why: The function wraps graph_brief in a try/except and returns "" on any exception.

observations.what: _HEADER_RESERVE is referenced but not defined in this chunk.
budget_chars is referenced but not defined in this chunk; it must be a parameter of graph_brief.
The budget check adds 1 for each line, but the header lines are not individually counted; the reserve is meant to cover that.
The comment about the 495-line symbol layer is a historical measurement; the current code limits neighbour symbols to public API only.
The render_brief docstring says 'or "" if there is nothing to say', but the function returns a non-empty string even when there are no structural facts (it includes a header saying so).
